title: System Security & Auth
html:
Comprehensive reference for OAuth2, OIDC, JWT signatures, refresh token rotation, web vulnerabilities (CSRF, CORS, XSS, SQLi), encryption, and RBAC/ABAC models.

OAuth 2.0 & OpenID Connect (OIDC)

Auth Code Flow with PKCE

Standard for Single Page Apps & Mobile. Client generates Code Verifier and Code Challenge. Prevents authorization code interception attacks without requiring client secret storage in browser.

OIDC (Identity Layer)

Built on top of OAuth 2.0. OAuth handles Authorization (Access Tokens); OIDC handles Authentication (ID Tokens containing user profile claims like sub, email).

JWT & Refresh Token Mechanics

JWT Structure: Header.Payload.Signature
• HS256: Symmetric key (shared secret between auth server & service).
• RS256: Asymmetric RSA key pair (Auth server signs with Private key, microservices verify with Public key).
• Refresh Token Rotation: Issuing a new refresh token with every refresh request. If an old refresh token is reused, system triggers security revoking ALL tokens for user.

Web Security Defenses

Vulnerability & Defense Matrix

Vulnerability Attack Mechanism Primary Defense
CSRF Unauthorized commands submitted from trusted user browser Anti-CSRF tokens, SameSite=Strict/Lax cookies
CORS Unauthorized cross-origin API requests Configure Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers
XSS Malicious JavaScript execution in victim browser Content Security Policy (CSP), Contextual output escaping
SQL Injection Injecting SQL syntax via untrusted user inputs Parameterized queries, Prepared statements, ORMs

Encryption: At Rest & In Transit

Encryption at Rest (KMS)

Envelope Encryption: Data encrypted with Data Encryption Key (DEK); DEK encrypted with Master Key (KEK) managed in Hardware Security Modules (AWS KMS).

Encryption in Transit (mTLS)

TLS 1.3 for external traffic. Mutual TLS (mTLS) inside Service Mesh: both client and server microservices authenticate each other's X.509 certificates.
